core_condition: at least one measured effect recorded in observed_effects from Ventora telemetry or public corpora

evidence.rationale: Deep and convergent. Asch (1956) conformity, Cialdini's focus theory of normative conduct (descriptive norms reliably shift behavior in field experiments), and applied evidence that online reviews/WOM measurably affect sales. One of the best-supported social-influence effects. Grade A- overall (not A) because it is strongly context-moderated, not a universal constant.

product_applicability.rationale: Directly implementable via usage counts, reviews, 'most popular', customer logos. Central to conversion surfaces. Reference at scale: Amazon reviews, SaaS trust logos.

measurability.rationale: Maps to cvr, tier_selection_distribution, trust-signal engagement — Amplitude-reachable and A/B-testable.

orthogonality.rationale: Distinct from ST-09 (others-as-evidence vs standing-relative-to-others) and SC-06 (consensus vs availability). Clear boundaries.

safety.rationale: Legitimate with real signals, but fake social proof — fabricated reviews, fake 'X viewing/bought', inflated counts — is a common dark pattern and specifically illegal (FTC endorsement guides, EU fake-review rules). Three hard rules block fabrication. Score 2: misuse is easy and regulated, mitigation is clear.

dissent: Two caveats discipline application. (1) The boomerang effect: telling people 'most others do X' can backfire if the norm is undesirable or if the user was already above the norm (Schultz et al. energy studies) — descriptive norms are not universally positive levers. (2) Fake-review and fake-activity literature shows consumers increasingly detect and penalize manufactured social proof, and it is now explicitly regulated. We claim the well-supported effect for genuine, relevant signals under uncertainty and hard-block fabrication.

evidence_sources.ref: Asch (1956). Studies of independence and conformity. Psychological Monographs 70(9).
Cialdini, Reno & Kallgren (1990). A focus theory of normative conduct. JPSP 58(6).

notes: Cross-checked against /corpora/evidence/SP-08.json (234 records; Asch and Cialdini pins resolved; WOM pin unresolved DOI but applied review literature present via terms). Verdict INCUBATING; CORE on a measured effect.
